readout_other: Two-photon calcium imaging (GCaMP6s) of V1 neurons through a cranial glass window; auditory brainstem response (ABR) testing used to confirm surgical deafening
direction_notes: Ultrasound directly and pressure-dependently activated a sparse population of ultrasound-sensitive neurons (UNs; up to 1.144% of neurons at 450 kPa) in V1 of deafened mice, independent of audition. When combined with visual stimulation, ultrasound bidirectionally modulated visual-sensitive neurons (VNs): one VN subgroup was inhibited by ultrasound (VNs2, p<0.0001) while another was excited (VNs3, p<0.0001), and a third was unaffected (VNs1).
safety_notes: Calculated mechanical index (MI = 0.45) at the maximum negative pressure of 450 kPa (1 MHz) was below the FDA limit of 1.9; ISPPA (6.75 W/cm2) and ISPTA (55.33 mW/cm2) at this pressure were well below FDA safety thresholds (190 W/cm2 and 720 mW/cm2 respectively); simulated focal temperature rise after 0.25 s of continuous ultrasound action at 450 kPa was approximately 0.055 degrees C.

exposures.label: Ultrasound stimulation of primary visual cortex (V1) through cranial glass window

device.model: custom annular ultrasound transducer integrated with 2-photon objective lens

timing.protocol_description: Smoothed ultrasonic pulses (sine-windowed to minimise auditory artifacts) were delivered through a cranial glass window to V1. At PRF 10 Hz: pulse duration (PD) 50 ms, pulse repetition interval (PRI) 100 ms, ramp duration (RD) 25 ms, stimulation duration (SD) 0.5 s (5 pulses), stimulation interval (SI) 30 s; each trial comprised 10 ultrasound stimulations (first discarded, 9 analysed). Pressure was varied (0, 69, 178, 315, 450 kPa) at fixed PRF 10 Hz; PRF was separately varied (2.5-2000 Hz) at a fixed pressure of 315 kPa to test auditory confound across cell types.

source_quotes.direction_notes: We found that UNs and VNs are two basically non-overlapping neuronal subpopulations, but ultrasound stimulation of V1 can inhibit or excite VNs. This shows that ultrasound-activated UNs can excite or inhibit VNs, and UNs may regulate VNs’ encoding of visual information.

flags.reason: Pressures were measured via hydrophone through a glass cranial window (using ex vivo mouse skull plus glass) rather than in free water alone; classified as in_situ (measurement) since this represents the field reaching the neurons, though the paper does not use the term 'in situ' itself.
ISPPA (6.75 W/cm2) is only explicitly reported for the maximum 450 kPa condition, not for the other tested pressures (69, 178, 315 kPa).

The main pressure-sweep experiments used a fixed PRF of 10 Hz; a separate experiment swept PRF (2.5-2000 Hz) at a fixed pressure of 315 kPa. Both parameter sweeps are combined into one exposure per the one-exposure-per-target-and-frequency rule, recorded as a list.

The paper describes 10 ultrasound stimulation trials per recording session but does not state whether individual mice underwent one or multiple separate imaging sessions/days across the various sub-experiments (pressure sweep, PRF sweep, hearing vs deaf comparisons).

39 mice total were used across viral injection/glass window/deafening procedures; individual sub-experiments report smaller overlapping cohort sizes in figure legends (e.g. n=7, n=8 mice per group) that could not be reliably summed without double-counting.

Anaesthesia (ketamine/xylazine) was used for surgical procedures (viral injection, glass window, deafening), but the paper does not explicitly state whether mice were awake or anaesthetised during the 2PCI/ultrasound stimulation sessions themselves.
